assessments.reasoning: The instrument allows distinguishing de jure vs. de facto female-headed households because sex of the household head is recorded (Q7, Q8) and marital status (Q19) is collected for all household members aged 12 and older, which can be combined with the presence or absence of a partner in the household roster. However, unpartnered mother-child units inside larger households cannot be identified because relationship to head (Q7) is collected relative only to the household head, without parent-child pointers on the roster. Women-maintained households or units cannot be identified through a main provider variable regardless of designated head, as no main provider question exists. Finally, the instrument does not link mother-child units to their own distinct consumption, production, or care activity (hearth-hold proxies).
